links.outcome: Reproducibility of ChatGPT-4 empathy labels and sentiment scores across three repeated runs
links.effect: Moderate reliability across repeated replies (Fleiss' kappa = 0.59; ICC = 0.62). Confusing or realization labels in 2.5% of outputs, with minor sentiment drift.
links.quote: Stability metrics indicated moderate reliability (κ = 0.59; ICC = 0.62), while occasional confusing or realization labels (2.5% of outputs) and minor sentiment drift underscored randomness as a risk.

links.outcome: Warmth, empathy and sentiment of ChatGPT-4 counseling replies, measured with NLP classifiers
links.effect: 97.5% warm responses, 94.2% empathy classification, mean compound sentiment 0.93 ± 0.19; automated proxies only, no clinician ratings.
links.quote: ChatGPT-4 achieved 97.5% warm responses, 94.2% empathy classification and a mean compound sentiment score of 0.93 ± 0.19.

screen.reason: The study tests the capabilities, empathy, and stability of ChatGPT-4 using simulated responses to 80 real college student counseling queries, but it does not compare outcomes with and without a specific guardrail or deployment practice.
